annotations.text:
THREE DIRECTIONS, NOT THREE SHADES

Each explores a different axis, and each would take the app somewhere the other two would not. Pick one and it becomes the whole app — every screen, not just this one.

The other page holds today's screens and the targeted fixes. That work stands whichever direction you pick; it is about defects, not about taste.

A · INSTRUMENT — what I would ship

One object is the interface. The 270° arc is the charge, the tick on it is your limit, the number sits inside it. Everything else is a hairline table — there is not a single card, shadow or rounded panel on the screen.

Space Grotesk with Geist Mono for every number. Cyan oklch(0.78 0.17 195) as the only accent; amber carries the battery because amber IS the state.

Motion earns its place: the arc sweeps to the value in 1.1s on a cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), the limit tick lands after it, rows rise in sequence. One reveal, then stillness.

WHY: a car is an instrument, and this is the only direction where the aesthetic and the data are the same decision. It also survives sunlight — hairlines and large type beat translucent panels outdoors, which is where this app is used.

TRADEOFF: austere. There is nothing decorative to like, so it lives or dies on the typography being right. And a 270° arc reads worse than a bar for fine differences — 24% vs 27% is not distinguishable at a glance.

Proven on a second screen beside it: the command set in the same language — no cards, values as a scale, state as a right-aligned mono label.

B · EDITORIAL

The data is set like print. Instrument Serif at 132px, a strict left column, hairline rules, actions as text with an arrow — no buttons at all. Warm near-black, single amber accent.

WHY: nothing else in the category looks like this, and it makes the app feel considered rather than technical. The serif numeral is genuinely beautiful at that size.

TRADEOFF: the boldest and the riskiest. Text-as-button is a real usability cost on a phone — nothing signals tappability except position, and a 48px text row is easy to miss while walking. It also fights the product: this is a utility you open for four seconds, not something you read.

C · AMBIENT

The field is the state: a soft radial light behind a wireframe car, amber when low, emerald while charging, breathing on a 7s loop. Controls are frosted glass floating at thumb height. Sora, thin weights, generous air.

WHY: this is what people mean by 'an app from the future', and it is the most immediately likeable of the three. State is legible before you read anything.

TRADEOFF: it is also the closest to what everyone else ships — glass and glow are the current default, so the distinctiveness fades fast. Translucency loses contrast in daylight, and a breathing glow behind a battery reading can read as decoration rather than information. If you pick this, the glow must always mean something.

TODAY, AND THE TARGETED FIXES

Rebuilt from the real components and tokens — Geist, the dark oklch ramp, 10/12/16px radii, 44px targets.

These fixes are defects, not taste: the car-asleep state that today deletes the screen, commands the car will refuse being offered confidently, the walking distance set at 11px grey. They are worth doing whichever direction wins.
